scenario:
You have volunteered for a research study about free-time activities.
You will have a short online interview with a researcher. The researcher will ask you some questions.

questions.question: Thank you for your participation. Today, I'd like to ask you some questions about free-time activities. First, in your opinion, what do people your age usually prefer to do in their free time—spend time outdoors, stay home with screens, or do something in between?
questions.modelAnswer: I think many people my age spend free time with screens, like streaming shows or playing games, because it is easy and social online. Still, a lot of friends also go outside for sports or short walks when the weather is nice. So I would say preferences are somewhere in between, with screens being a bit more common on weekdays.
evaluationPoints: Addresses free-time preferences of people a similar age
Chooses outdoors, screens, or in between
Gives at least one reason or example
Stays on topic within the time limit

questions.question: I see. And what do you usually do after a long, busy day—do you rest quietly, meet friends, or try to be productive?
questions.modelAnswer: After a long day I usually rest quietly at first. I like to listen to music or watch a short video to clear my mind. If I still have energy, I might message a friend or go for a brief walk. I only try to be productive when I have an urgent deadline the next morning.
evaluationPoints: States a clear personal after-work or after-class habit
Chooses rest, social time, productivity, or a mix
Explains why that choice fits a busy day

questions.question: Interesting. Many people say that modern technology has changed how we relax. Do you think people today have more meaningful free time than in the past? Why or why not?
questions.modelAnswer: I do not think free time is always more meaningful today. Technology gives us more options, but it also creates constant distraction and pressure to stay online. In the past, free time might have been simpler, like reading or talking face to face. Those activities can feel deeper. Still, technology helps people learn hobbies and connect across distance, so the result depends on how we use it.
evaluationPoints: Takes a clear yes/no or nuanced position
Connects free time to modern technology
May briefly acknowledge the other side

questions.question: Good points. I just have one more question. Some people believe that sharing hobbies with family is an important way to stay close. Do you agree, or do you think close relationships can be built in other ways? Why?
questions.modelAnswer: I agree that shared hobbies help families stay close, but they are not the only way. Doing activities together creates memories and common topics to talk about. However, families can also stay close through daily conversations, supporting each other during hard times, and celebrating small routines. So hobbies help, but care and communication matter even more.
evaluationPoints: Responds clearly to the agree/or-other-ways frame
Gives a reason for the chosen position
May mention hobbies and alternative ways to connect
